pages.raw_text: Agent Plugins / Coding Agents / Claude Code Claude Code Persistent cross-session memory for Claude Code. Connect Negentro to your coding agent so relevant context can persist across sessions and become available when you need it. ✓ Current plugin version: v1.2.0 Prerequisites 01 Negentro account / API key — required to authenticate requests. Set it as NEGENTRO_API_KEY , 02 Supported agent environment — Claude Code CLI must be installed and accessible on your path. 03 Required runtime/CLI dependencies — Node.js 18+ and negentro-cli . Quick start Copy export NEGENTRO_API_KEY = "your-api-key" negentro plugin install claude-code negentro plugin status This installs the plugin, wires it into your Claude Code session, and confirms the connection is active. 1 Install 2 Configure 3 Restart agent 4 Verify Managing the plugin Copy negentro plugin install claude-code negentro plugin update claude-code negentro plugin uninstall claude-code negentro plugin status What you can do Automatic memory Captures relevant context from coding sessions automatically, without manual intervention. Commands Explicit commands for searching, checking status, forgetting, and pausing/resuming memory capture. Search tool Search previous sessions and retrieve relevant context on demand. Sidekick agent Run isolated investigation or implementation work while preserving the primary context. Commands COMMAND WHAT IT DOES /memory:search Search memories from earlier sessions. /memory:status Check current memory/configuration state. /memory:forget Delete or forget selected memories. /memory:pause Pause automatic memory capture. /memory:resume Resume automatic memory capture. /memory:remember Explicitly capture something important. Search tool Use the search tool to query prior sessions and retrieve context matched by relevance and scope. memory.search("authentication flow", { scope: "project" }) { "results" : [ { "memory_id" : "mem_123" , "content" : "Authentication uses JWT tokens for the main API..." , "score" : 0.91 } ] } Sidekick agent The sidekick agent handles isolated investigation or implementation work in a separate context, then returns findings to the main agent without polluting its working memory. 01 Main Agent → 02 Sidekick → 03 Investigation → 04 Result → 05 Main Agent How it works 01 Agent Session → 02 Capture → 03 Negentro Memory → 04 Extract → 05 Store → 06 Recall → 07 Next Session 01 Capture — capture relevant activity from the agent session. 02 Flush — send captured context to Negentro after meaningful interaction boundaries. 03 Extract — identify useful info such as project context, decisions, constraints, preferences. 04 Recall — retrieve relevant memories during a later session. Memory scoping Memory is scoped between shared project context and personal context, with relevant overlap surfaced during retrieval. Current Request Continue the authentication work PERSONAL MEMORY Preferences • History • Goals Context Assembly Retrieve • Filter • Combine PROJECT MEMORY Codebase • Decisions • Files SESSION CONTEXT Current task • Recent activity • Conversation RELEVANT CONTEXT Only what the current task needs Search scope SCOPE WHAT YOU GET repo Project memory. dir Directory-specific context. user Personal memory. session Current session context. Example: setting scope to dir narrows retrieval to memories captured within the current working directory only. Settings SETTING DEFAULT WHAT IT CONTROLS api_key none Authenticates requests to Negentro. user_id none Identifies the memory owner. top_k 5 Number of memories returned per search. max_content_chars 4000 Max characters captured per memory. search_scope repo Default scope used for retrieval. telemetry true Enables anonymous usage telemetry. Copy export NEGENTRO_API_KEY = "..." export NEGENTRO_USER_ID = "..." export NEGENTRO_SEARCH_SCOPE = "repo" Upgrading Before upgrading to a new plugin version, walk through the checklist below to avoid breaking existing configuration or memory behavior. ✓ Review changed configuration ✓ Check command changes ✓ Verify memory compatibility ✓ Re-run plugin setup ✓ Confirm agent compatibility Troubleshooting PROBLEM FIX Missing API key Configure the Negentro API key and restart the plugin. Unauthorized Verify the API key and account permissions. No memory after session Check that memory capture is enabled and that the plugin completed its session flush. Plugin won't start Verify the supported agent version and plugin installation. Search returns nothing Check the active search scope and confirm memories exist for that scope. Telemetry What may be collected Event type Plugin version Runtime information Basic performance/error metadata Document the exact telemetry behavior here before production release. export NEGENTRO_TELEMETRY=false Copy Related agent plugins Negentro MCP Connect Negentro memory through MCP-compatible agent workflows. → Codex Integration Add persistent context to supported Codex workflows. → Cursor Persistent memory for Cursor. → OpenCode Context-aware OpenCode workflows. → Gemini CLI Memory for Gemini CLI agents. → Cline Persistent context for Cline. → Building with Negentro? pages.title: LiveKit Agent Harness
pages.lead: Connect LiveKit Agents framework with pre-warmed participant context and automatic speech transcription ingestion.

code_blocks.code:
from livekit.agents import JobContext
from piyapi import PiyAPIClient

piyapi = PiyAPIClient(api_key="sk_live_your_key_here")

async def on_participant_joined(participant):
    mems = piyapi.memories.search(query="preferences", user_id=participant.identity)
    print(f"Loaded {len(mems)} historical memories for {participant.identity}")

pages.title: Plugin Overview
pages.lead: Negentro Agent Plugins enable AI agents to maintain cross-session memory, access unified context assembly, and query previous interactions without polluting token windows.
pages.raw_text: Agent Plugins / Plugin Resources / Overview Plugin Overview Architecture and capabilities of Negentro Agent Plugins. Negentro Agent Plugins enable AI agents to maintain cross-session memory, access unified context assembly, and query previous interactions without polluting token windows. Core Pillars 1. Bitemporal Graph Memory Stores both valid time (when the fact was true in the real world) and transaction time (when the system recorded it), allowing precise version rollbacks. 2. UnifiedScorer Retrieval Combines dense HNSW vector similarity, sparse BM25 text match, recency decay, and relation graphs for high-precision retrieval. 3. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Standard stdio transport providing 30 native tools for Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Desktop, and CLI agents. ← PREVIOUS: Claude Code NEXT: Installation →

pages.title: Memory Architecture
pages.raw_text: Agent Plugins / Plugin Resources / Memory Memory Architecture Bitemporal memory lifecycle and context scoping. The 4-Step Lifecycle 01 Capture: Records agent conversation turns, edits, and tool results. 02 Flush: Dispatches payloads at interaction boundaries or idle triggers. 03 Extract: LLM extractor parses key technical decisions, constraints, and dependencies. 04 Recall: UnifiedScorer fetches context when new prompts are submitted. ← PREVIOUS: Commands NEXT: Troubleshooting →
